sources.news_title: Quebec pilot who died in Remembrance Day plane crash identified
sources.text:
A crashed aircraft lies behind a house in St-Georges de Beauce, Que., Wednesday, Nov. 11, 2026. Quebec provincial police say one person is dead after a plane crashed south of Quebec City at around 11 a.m. THE CANADIAN PRESS/Jacques Boissinot
MONTREAL - The pilot who died in a Remembrance Day plane crash south of Quebec City has been identified.
The Quebec coroner’s office named the victim on Thursday as 68-year-old Daniel Parent of St-Georges, Que.
Parent was taking part in a Remembrance Day commemoration with other pilots when his aircraft went down near the St-Georges airport.
ARTICLE CONTINUES BELOW
The City of St-Georges said Parent was a member of the local Beauce flying club, and offered condolences to his family, the wider aviation community and to any veterans who were affected.
Flags have been lowered to half-mast at city hall and the airport, it said.
The Transportation Safety Board said Parent was flying his single-engine Mooney aircraft in formation with five other planes when the crash occurred.
Spokesperson Nic Defalco said the plane broke away from the others as a planned part of the show, but was unable to rejoin them.
“When attempting to rejoin the formation, the aircraft passed beneath the other aircraft and continued on that trajectory, ultimately crashing into a wooded area,” Defalco said.
Defalco said two investigators were at the scene on Thursday, and that it was too soon to hypothesize about what caused the crash.
Provincial police spokesperson Audrey-Anne Bilodeau said officers were meeting witnesses on Thursday. She said the force is still investigating for criminal elements, though she said crashes like this are rarely linked to a crime.
She said a coroner is also investigating the causes and circumstances surrounding the death.
This report by The Canadian Press was first published Nov. 12, 2026.

sources.news_title: Pilot killed in plane crash during Remembrance Day ceremony in Quebec
sources.text:
Canada News
Pilot killed in plane crash during Remembrance Day ceremony in Quebec
Floyd Brenz., Philippine Canadian Inquirer
November 12, 2026
A Remembrance Day commemoration in Saint-Georges, Quebec, ended in tragedy after one of the aircraft taking part in a ceremonial flyover crashed near the local airport, killing its pilot.
The crash happened at around 11 a.m. Wednesday in a wooded area near the airport, about 100 kilometres south of Quebec City.
Quebec provincial police said the victim was a man in his 60s who was the only person aboard the aircraft. Local reports identified him as 68-year-old Daniel Parent, a member of the Club Aéronautique de Beauce flying club.
Saint-Georges Mayor Manon Bougie said six aircraft were performing a Missing Man formation during the city’s Remembrance Day ceremony when one of the planes went down.
The aircraft reportedly crashed while approaching the airport for landing and caught fire. Emergency responders arrived within minutes but were unable to save the pilot.
A resident living near the crash site said he heard a loud metallic noise before seeing flames in the wooded area. He attempted to help using fire extinguishers but said the blaze was too large.
The tragedy prompted an outpouring of condolences from Quebec and federal officials, as the community mourned the loss of a local pilot on a day dedicated to remembering those who served in the military.
The Transportation Safety Board of Canada is sending investigators to examine the wreckage and determine what caused the crash. Authorities have not yet established the circumstances behind the incident.

sources.news_title: Pilot Dead After Plane Involved in Remembrance Day Ceremony Crashes Near Quebec City
sources.text:
A pilot has died after a small plane crashed Nov. 11 near Quebec City, where it was scheduled to take part in a Remembrance Day ceremony.
Quebec provincial police have confirmed the pilot was pronounced dead at the scene. The Sûreté du Québec is investigating.
The crash occurred near the Saint-Georges airport in the Beauce region, about 100 kilometres south of Quebec City.
Quebec Premier Paul St-Pierre Plamondon confirmed in a Nov. 11 social media post that an aircraft scheduled to take part in Remembrance Day commemorations had crashed earlier that morning in Saint-Georges-de-Beauce.
He said he was monitoring the situation and was in contact with Public Safety Minister Guy Jr. Lapointe to determine whether the provincial government could provide assistance.
“At this time, we do not know whether the pilot or anyone else has been injured. My heart goes out to those involved and their families,” St-Pierre Plamondon said.
In an online post, Quebec Liberal Leader Charles Milliard offered his condolences to the family and loved ones of the pilot who died in the crash, saying his thoughts were with everyone affected by the tragedy.
Saint-Georges Mayor Manon Bougie issued a statement Nov. 11 confirming that the plane crashed at about 11:01 a.m. near the Saint-Georges airport. She said the fire department reported that the aircraft crashed in a wooded area and caught fire on impact.
Bougie said the crash reportedly occurred as the pilot was approaching the airport to land, after taking part in a Remembrance Day ceremony.
“What has just happened is truly sad and terrible,” Bougie said. “Our hearts go out to the family and loved ones affected by this tragedy. All our thoughts and prayers are with them at this time.”
Bougie added that representatives of the Transportation Safety Board of Canada were on their way to the crash site, while the Sûreté du Québec was taking over communications about the incident.
Federal Transport Minister Steven MacKinnon said in a social media post that he was saddened to learn of the pilot’s death.
“My thoughts are with his family, his loved ones, and everyone affected by this tragedy,” he remarked.
Conservative Party Leader Pierre Poilievre wrote on social media that his thoughts were with the pilot’s family and loved ones, and he also thanked “the courageous emergency teams who responded to the call.”
A spokesperson for the Transportation Safety Board said in an email to The Epoch Times that the agency has deployed investigators to the site to gather information and assess the occurrence.
On site, they will gather information on a number of things, including but not limited to the aircraft wreckage, the aircraft’s operation and human factors, the operator/company, meteorological conditions, the aircraft’s maintenance history, and any other relevant information.

sources.news_title: Quebec pilot killed in plane crash during Remembrance Day aerial ceremony
Pilot of Quebec plane scheduled for Remembrance Day ceremony killed in crash
sources.text:
A Remembrance Day ceremony south of Quebec City ended in tragedy Wednesday when a pilot died in a small plane crash after taking part in an aerial salute.
The plane went down after completing a flypast with five other aircraft, part of an annual tradition in Saint-Georges, a small city about 100 kilometres from the provincial capital.
The victim, a man in his 60s, was part of a group of local pilots who perform the same aerial formation every year, said Mayor Manon Bougie.
“It’s terrible,” she said. “Remembrance Day will never be the same for us.”
Ms. Bougie said a small crowd had assembled for the ceremony, and watched as the six planes flew past. They performed the Missing Man formation, in which one aircraft pulls away from the others, leaving a gap to commemorate fallen soldiers.
Everything seemed normal at the time, Ms. Bougie said. But shortly afterward, emergency vehicles started driving past in the direction of the airport.
She later learned the plane had crashed as it was preparing to land, catching fire and sending up a column of smoke. She also learned the victim was the pilot who detached from the Missing Man formation. “It’s the height of irony,” she said.
Provincial police have not confirmed the identity of the pilot.
The Canadian Press
Yvon Thibodeau, a member of the Royal Canadian Legion who attended the ceremony, said the pilots are members of a local group called the Club Aéronautique de Beauce. He said it’s mostly the same pilots who perform the formation each year.
“They practise a lot in the summer,” he said. “You often see them going by.”
The Department of National Defence has confirmed that the plane did not belong to the Royal Canadian Air Force, and the pilot was not a member of the Canadian Armed Forces.
Sergeant Audrey-Anne Bilodeau, a spokesperson for the provincial police force, said the crash occurred in a wooded area near the airport at around 11 a.m., and the pilot was pronounced dead at the scene.
Key moments from Remembrance Day across Canada
She said the pilot was alone in the plane and no one else was injured.
Mr. Thibodeau said the host of the event, a retired lieutenant-colonel who was one of the pilots in years past, received the news of the crash and shared it with the crowd.
“He started crying because it was one of his close friends,” Mr. Thibodeau said. “He broke down.”
Ms. Bougie said many of the people in attendance seemed to be in shock upon hearing the news. “There was definitely confusion,” she said. “The situation seemed unreal – it was impossible to imagine it happening.”
Quebec Premier Paul St-Pierre Plamondon addressed the incident in a social media post, saying he is in contact with the province’s domestic security minister.
“I would like to offer my sincere condolences to his family and loved ones,” he said of the pilot.
The Transportation Safety Board of Canada said Wednesday afternoon that investigators were on their way to the site.

sources.news_title: Pilot dead in Quebec crash was returning from Remembrance Day ceremony
sources.text:
Pilot killed in crash upon returning from Remembrance Day ceremony south of Quebec City
Posted November 11, 2026 1:22 pm.
A pilot returning to the airport after participating in a Remembrance Day ceremony has died in a plane crash in a town south of Quebec City.
The small aircraft crashed into a wooded area near the airport in Saint-Georges, in Quebec’s Beauce region, around 11:01 a.m. Wednesday.
The pilot has been identified by the Sûreté du Québec as a man in his 60s who lived in the region. A spokesperson for the provincial police, Audrey-Anne Bilodeau, says he was the lone occupant of the plane and he was declared dead at the scene.
“What has just happened is truly sad and terrible,” said Saint-Georges Mayor Manon Bougie in a news release. “Our hearts go out to the family and loved ones affected by this tragedy. All our thoughts and prayers are with them at this time.”
The municipality of Saint-Georges says the crash appears to have happened while the pilot was preparing to land, and the plane reportedly caught fire upon impact.
Bilodeau says it is too early in the investigation to confirm those exact details.
“Regarding all the circumstances, whether it happened during landing or takeoff, there are many questions you might be asking,” Bilodeau told reporters. “Was there an operational error, or was there a mechanical failure in the aircraft? You will understand that the investigation will reveal this, working in conjunction with our partners at the Transportation Safety Board (TSB).”
The TSB indeed dispatched a team of investigators to the scene, which is about 100 kilometres south of Quebec City.
“Their expertise lies precisely in determining whether there was a breakage, a mechanical failure, or an operational error that could have led to a loss of control — resulting in the tragic outcome,” the SQ spokesperson said.
Bilodeau said the police force will speak to witnesses. She said she could not speak to the pilot’s level of experience.
Politicians across Quebec and the country extended their condolences to the pilot and his family.
In a post on X, Quebec Premier Paul St-Pierre Plamondon said he is in contact with Quebec Domestic Security Minister Guy Jr. Lapointe “to obtain further details and to determine whether the Government of Quebec can provide any assistance.”
The leader of the Quebec Liberal Party, Charles Milliard, offered his condolences to the pilot’s family and loved ones. “My thoughts are with everyone affected by this tragedy,” he wrote on X.
At the federal level, Quebec lieutenant Joël Lightbound said: “On this day, as we pay tribute to those who have served us, my thoughts are with the pilot’s family, his loved ones, and the entire Beauce region.”
Federal Transport Minister Steven MacKinnon said he was saddened to hear of the pilot’s passing.
The leader of the Conservative Party of Canada, Pierre Poilievre, also expressed his sympathies. “Thank you to the courageous emergency responders who answered the call,” he said on X.
–With files from La Presse Canadienne

Pilot dead after Remembrance Day aircraft crashes in Quebec

Quebec provincial police (SQ) said the crash happened at around 11 a.m. and there was only one person aboard the aircraft.
The pilot was declared dead at the scene. Police said there were no other victims.
The crash involved a small aircraft that had just participated in a Remembrance Day commemoration, the City of Saint-Georges said in a statement.
SQ spokesperson Audrey-Anne Bilodeau said the pilot had been flying with a group of other planes when his aircraft went down.
The small plane came down in a wooded area near the Saint-Georges airport and caught fire after the crash, the city said. The crash happened as the pilot was approaching the airport to land.
Police identified the victim as a man in his 60s who lived in the region.

“I thought, ‘Where is it going?’” Maheux said. “Then it disappeared into the trees, and I saw a ball of fire, followed by black smoke.”
“It all happened in three seconds.”

St-Pierre Plamondon said he was working with the province’s domestic security minister to gather more information about what happened.

sources.news_title: Pilot identified after fatal crash during Remembrance Day ceremony near Quebec City
sources.text: A pilot has died after a small plane involved in a Remembrance Day ceremony crashed Wednesday in Quebec. A source confirmed to CTV News the pilot was 68-year-old Daniel Parent. Earlier in the day Wednesday, Quebec provincial police said he was pronounced dead at the scene. The crash happened at around 11 a.m. in a wooded area near the Saint-Georges airport in Beauce, about 100 kilometres south of Quebec City. “It’s a major crime unit that is investigating the case, trying to make sure that there was no criminal aspect involved,” said Sureté du Québec (SQ) spokesperson Audrey-Anne Bilodeau, adding that the Transport Safety Board is also heading to the scene. “It was participating in an event with other planes when he went down, unfortunately,” said Bilodeau. Planes were performing aerial salute Bilodeau said the pilot, who was from the Saint-Georges area, was alone in the plane. Manon Bougie, the mayor of Saint-Georges, told CTV News that the plane was part of a formation of six planes taking part in the city’s Remembrance Day ceremony Wednesday morning. The planes were performing a “Missing Man” formation, an aerial salute that is performed during commemorative events to honour a fallen soldier. The plane was on its final approach for landing when it crashed. “This is a very sad and tragic event, especially on a day dedicated to remembrance and reflection,” the mayor said. “Our thoughts are with the victim’s family and loved ones, as well as everyone affected by this tragedy.” A witness told Noovo Info that the plane apparently broke away from the group of other aircraft flying as part of the ceremony. A woman who witnessed the events from her office window noticed that the plane was flying lower than the others before disappearing behind some trees. Black smoke was then reportedly seen rising into the sky. Another witness saw the plane nosedive. Political leaders offer condolences Political leaders in Quebec offered their condolences to the pilot’s family. Quebec Premier Paul St-Pierre Plamondon said he is closely monitoring the situation with Domestic Security Minister Guy Jr. Lapointe. “I would like to offer my sincere condolences to his family and loved ones,” the premier said in a post on X. Quebec Liberal leader Charles Milliard also reacted to the tragedy. “My deepest condolences go out to the family and loved ones of the pilot who tragically lost his life in the crash of this aircraft in Saint-Georges-de-Beauce while taking part in Remembrance Day celebrations,” he wrote on X. “My thoughts are with everyone affected by this tragedy.”

sources.news_title: Quebec Plane Crash Kills Pilot After Remembrance Flypast
sources.text:
A Quebec plane crash during a Remembrance Day tribute has killed a pilot in the town of Saint-Georges, in the Beauce region of Canada. The small aircraft was one of six planes that flew over the town’s ceremony on Wednesday, 11 November. It went down in a wooded area near Saint-Georges airport at about 11 a.m. local time, according to CTV News and Quebec provincial police.
The pilot was alone on board. Police confirmed that he died at the scene. His name has not been officially released, and the type of aircraft has not been made public.
What happened in the Quebec plane crash
Saint-Georges is a city of about 33,000 people, roughly 100 kilometres south of Quebec City. On Wednesday morning, residents gathered at Place des vétérans for the annual Remembrance Day service.
Six light aircraft flew over the ceremony in a “Missing Man” formation, Mayor Manon Bougie told local media. After the flypast, the planes headed back towards the local airport. According to the mayor, one aircraft crashed while it was on final approach to land.
The plane came down in woods behind homes near Parc des Sept-Chutes, close to the airport. It caught fire, and a tall column of black smoke could be seen from a distance. Police, firefighters and paramedics rushed to the site and set up a security perimeter.
What witnesses said
Witnesses quoted by the Quebec broadcaster Noovo Info gave early accounts. One said the plane broke away from the group and flew lower than the others before it disappeared behind the trees. Another described seeing the aircraft dive nose-first.
These are eyewitness descriptions only. Investigators have not said what caused the crash, and early accounts often change as evidence is examined.
Police and safety investigators respond
The Sûreté du Québec (SQ), the provincial police, confirmed the death on Wednesday afternoon. Early reports had suggested the pilot was taken to hospital in serious condition. Police later clarified that he had died at the scene.
SQ spokesperson Audrey-Anne Bilodeau said the plane “was participating in an event with other planes” when it went down. She added that the force’s major crimes unit is investigating. This is a routine step to rule out any criminal element in a sudden death.
The Transportation Safety Board of Canada (TSB) has also sent investigators to the site, according to Canadian media reports.
How a TSB investigation works
The TSB is Canada’s independent accident investigation agency. Its job is to find out what happened and why, so that similar accidents can be prevented. It does not assign blame or decide civil or criminal liability.
In a typical light-aircraft investigation, the team will:
- document the wreckage and the site before anything is moved;
- review the aircraft’s maintenance records and the pilot’s licence and experience;
- gather weather data, radio recordings and any video from the ceremony;
- interview the other pilots in the formation and witnesses on the ground.
Small private aircraft usually carry no flight data recorder. As a result, investigators often rely more on wreckage analysis, engine examination and witness evidence. A final report can take many months.
Tributes from the community and leaders
News of the crash reached the crowd while the ceremony was still under way. Mayor Bougie was too shaken to deliver her prepared speech. She later called it a very sad and tragic event and sent her thoughts to the pilot’s family.
Quebec Premier Paul St-Pierre Plamondon offered his condolences on X. He said he was following the situation with the province’s domestic security minister. Quebec Liberal leader Charles Milliard also sent his sympathy to the family.
Background: the Missing Man formation
The Missing Man formation is a traditional aerial salute. It honours pilots and service members who have died. Aircraft fly over a memorial in a tight group, and one position is either left empty or one aircraft climbs away from the group. The gap represents those who did not come home.
Remembrance Day on 11 November marks the end of the First World War in 1918. Across Canada, towns hold ceremonies with wreath-laying, a minute of silence and, in some places, flypasts by military or civilian aircraft. The tragedy is all the more painful because it happened during an event meant to honour the fallen.
Why formation flying needs care
Formation flights look graceful from the ground, but they are demanding for pilots. Aircraft fly close together at low height and must keep careful spacing. Pilots also have to manage the break-up of the group and a safe return to the airfield.
For this reason, aviation authorities in most countries require briefings, practice and approvals for flypasts at public events. It is not yet known whether any of these factors played a part on Wednesday.
Lessons for light aviation in Nepal
Nepal does not have a large private flying community like Canada’s. Even so, flypasts and display flights take place during national events, and light aircraft and helicopters operate daily in demanding terrain. The same safety principles apply: clear planning, strong briefings and a culture of reporting risks.
The Civil Aviation Authority of Nepal (CAAN) has recently been reviewing safety after the Pheriche helicopter collision in Solukhumbu. Independent investigation, as practised by the TSB, is also central to that process. Readers can also follow our coverage of the Learjet 60 crash investigation in Florida.
What’s next
- The TSB will examine the wreckage and decide the scope of its investigation.
- The SQ’s major crimes unit will complete its inquiry into the circumstances of the death.
- Officials are expected to confirm the aircraft type and the pilot’s identity in the coming days.
Aviation Nepal will update this story as verified information becomes available. Our thoughts are with the pilot’s family and the people of Saint-Georges.

sources.news_title: Pilot of Aircraft in Canadian Remembrance Day Ceremony Dies in Crash
sources.text:
Aeronautical chart of St-Georges Airport in Quebec. [Credit: SkyVector]
Key Takeaways:
A pilot involved in Canadian Remembrance Day commemorations died in a plane crash on Wednesday in St-Georges-de-Beauce, Quebec.
The small aircraft crashed near St-Georges Airport after participating in a ceremony, with witnesses reporting it separated from other planes, nosedived, and exploded.
The Transportation Safety Board of Canada is investigating the incident, and Quebec officials have offered condolences to the pilot's family and loved ones.
The pilot of an aircraft linked to Canadian Remembrance Day commemorations has died following a crash in Quebec’s St-Georges-de-Beauce, according to Quebec Premier Paul St-Pierre Plamondon. It is unclear if there were any passengers aboard the airplane.
Canada’s CTV News reported that the crash occurred Wednesday around 11 a.m. EST in a wooded area near St-Georges Airport (CYSG) in Beauce. According to the Montreal Gazette, the aircraft was approaching to land at the airport with five other aircraft after taking part in a ceremony.
